educationalGoal: The aim of this course is to help you develop the skills necessary for you to make the transition to a KIT student. After completing this course, you will be familiar with KIT’s academic support systems and be able to utilize them for self-management, which will provide motivation to engage in learning activities in KIT actively and get on a path to a meaningful and successful career.
advice: 1. Presidential lecture: Comprehending the meaning and significance of “KIT IDEALS” and the “Student Pledge” to raise awareness and consciousness as a KIT student. 2. “Weekly report”: Making good use of KIT’s academic support system to practice self-management. 3. “Newspaper portfolio”: Raising interest in social issues. 4. Counseling center lecture: Discovering our character strengths for career management. 5. Academic writing exercise: Improving writing skills by writing essays. 6. Group discussions and presentations: Improving discussion and presentation skills. 7. Academic planning: Comprehending KIT’s educational programs (Humanities and Social Sciences Program, English Language Program, Mathematics and Science Program, Practical Engineering Program, and other specialized programs) and systems. 8. Interview with the academic advisor about living and learning conditions. *The submission date for each assignments must be strictly observed. *Access the “Student Portal”, “e-syllabus”, and other systems frequently to get the latest information.
requiredKnowledge: 1. Willpower to understand and observe “KIT IDEALS.” 2. Willpower to understand and observe the “Student Pledge.” 3. Willpower to acquire KIT human skills. 4. Motivation and willpower to study and learn by yourself.

activityGoals.body: Be able to improve self-management skills and establish a learning attitude through a weekly report.
Be able to increase your interest in social issues and career design through news reports.
Be able to organize the contents of special lectures accurately and express your opinions in academic writing.
Be able to learn the basic techniques of academic writing and create sentences according to the rules.
Be able to compare and summarize opinions in group discussions, and express them in speech and writing.
Be able to clarify future learning goals and plan for the second semester.

achievementLevels.ideal: Be able to create a “Weekly report” and describe your goals clearly. Be able to create a “Newspaper portfolio” to show awareness of your career design. Be able to organize special lecture issues and express your opinion about the lecture questions. Be able to understand the basics of academic writing and create precise and clear academic texts according to the rules. Be able to express your opinions in comparison with others in speech and writing. Be able to have a positive attitude toward learning, such as attending classes and meeting deadlines.
achievementLevels.standard: Be able to create a “Weekly report”. Be able to create a “Newspaper portfolio”. Be able to organize special lecture issues. Be able to write academic texts according to the rules. Be able to distinguish your opinions from others. Be able to have a learning attitude, such as attending classes and meeting deadlines.
